# A timeline grid's header edge changes colour where the timeline starts

## Context

Owned for the Engine 14 cut (Mon 2026-11-23), so no curated contributor labels: `neo-theme-neo-dark` is the Portal's default theme, so every Gantt and scheduler example in the v14 showcase carries this seam. Promoted by triage from my defect-note `da4c6400` (2026-11-21 09:48Z), re-measured below.

## The Problem

On `dev` `5c8d14ab26`, 1440 × 900, `neo-theme-neo-dark`, computed styles:

| Example | Plain/tree header button, bottom border | Timeline header, bottom edge | Edge y |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/scheduler/basic` | `1px solid rgb(29, 46, 98)` | `inset 0 -1px rgb(38, 47, 61)` | 133 |
| `examples/gantt/basic` | `1px solid rgb(29, 46, 98)` | `inset 0 -1px rgb(38, 47, 61)` | 121 |

The header's bottom edge sits on one pixel row, as #21679 AC-2 requires, but it changes colour where the timeline starts: navy `#1D2E62` under the plain columns, slate `#262f3d` under the timeline. The plain columns' body cells draw their row line in the same navy (`1px rgb(29, 46, 98)`). The change of colour is visible at 1× and 2× DPR.

## The Architectural Reality

- Before #21772, one rule drew the whole header/body boundary: `resources/css/src/grid/header/Toolbar.css:2`, `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--grid-container-border-color);`. The timeline header's own slate `border-bottom` sat one pixel above it.
- #21772 (resolving #21679, steps 3 and 4) moved the boundary onto the header items so the now line crosses it. Plain/tree buttons colour their border with `--grid-container-border-color` (`resources/css/src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css:5-10`). The timeline header draws `box-shadow: inset 0 -1px var(--neo-timeline-border-color)` (`:20`, and `:43` on `:hover`). Step 3 kept the token of the old timeline border. That border was a line above the boundary; the inset now IS the boundary under the timeline, so it replaced the grid's colour there.
- Token values: `neo-dark` `--grid-container-border-color: var(--purple-800)` (`#1D2E62`) vs `--neo-timeline-border-color: #262f3d`; `neo-light` `#ddd` vs `#d5dbe3`. `dark`, `light` and `cyberpunk` give both tokens one value. `examples/scheduler/meridian` maps them to `--mer-grid` and `--mer-line`, so it draws the same seam. `apps/workstation` maps both to `--workstation-line`.
- Design authority: `resources/css/src/grid/header/Toolbar.css:2`, "border-bottom: 1px solid var(--grid-container-border-color);": the grid's header/body boundary is one line in the grid's border colour. This amends the token choice of my own #21679 step 3, not its geometry.

## The Fix

- `resources/css/src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css`: the timeline header's bottom-edge inset (`:20` at rest, `:43` on `:hover`) uses `var(--grid-container-border-color)`.
- The scale's own lines keep `--neo-timeline-border-color`: the tier separator (`.neo-timeline-header-major`, `:67`) and the scheduler's vertical separators (`resources/css/src/scheduler/Container.css:7-8`).
- `test/playwright/e2e/gantt/NowLine.spec.mjs`: the arm that checks the shared bottom edge also asserts that the timeline header's edge colour equals the plain button's bottom border colour. It runs in both themes, at rest and on `:hover`, and is red on `dev` first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: In `examples/gantt/basic` and `examples/scheduler/basic`, in `neo-theme-neo-dark` and `neo-theme-neo-light`, the timeline header's bottom-edge colour equals the plain header buttons' bottom border colour, at rest and on `:hover`. Pinned in `NowLine.spec.mjs`, red on `dev` `5c8d14ab26`.
- [ ] AC-2: #21679's arms still pass: the now line meets the first row's segment with a `0px` gap, and every bottom edge shares one pixel row with toolbars and bodies unmoved.
- [ ] AC-3: Before/after frames of the boundary at 2× DPR in `neo-dark`, plus one whole 1440 × 900 frame.

## Out of Scope

- Either token's value in any theme.
- The scale's own lines: the tier separator and the tick separators.
- `grid/header/Toolbar.css` for grids without a timeline (#21679's Avoided Traps).

## Avoided Traps

- Setting neo-dark's `--neo-timeline-border-color` to the grid's value: it also colours the scale's tick lines, which stay as they are, and Meridian would still differ.
- Plain buttons taking the timeline token: the plain columns' row lines below them are the grid's token, so the edge would leave their family instead.
